name: alakazam_ml_v34
model: The unchanged v31 safety and exact-memory shell followed by a 657-feature large-leaf LambdaRank model. The teacher submission was refetched for 980 further games, the oldest eighth of the enlarged corpus is dropped, and the deployed tree count is chosen by validation Top-1 instead of by NDCG early stopping.
model_scope: The learned policy covers unseen single-choice MAIN decisions. Exact Majkel memory answers previously recorded boards; v29 and the deterministic policy remain the fallbacks for unsupported, unsafe, low-time, or illegal cases.
changed_versus_v33: Teacher submission 54773249 refetched: 980 further games, corpus 1288 -> 2268 episodes.
Holdout re-cut chronologically because every new game postdates the v33 frozen holdout.
Training corpus limited to the most recent 87.5% of episodes.
Deployed tree count selected by validation Top-1 instead of LightGBM NDCG early stopping: 1005 -> 2050.
unchanged_from_v33: Turn-order graded relevance labels (chosen 7 / next 3 / later 1 / unplayed 0).
v29 fallback, Majkel board memory, all five v31 safety guards, runtime decision logic.

holdout_identity.note: The 980 refetched games are all chronologically newer than the v33 frozen holdout, so that holdout cannot be reused for v34 without training on games that postdate the test block. The holdout was re-cut chronologically and the v33 configuration was refitted on its own training episodes to produce a comparable baseline on it.

teacher_training.label_definition: turn_order_graded_relevance: chosen 7, played at the next decision 3, played later in the same turn 1, not played 0

versus_v33_same_holdout.baseline_definition: The v33 configuration refitted on exactly the episodes v33 could train on (its own 984 pre-boundary episodes), scored on the v34 chronological holdout.
versus_v33_same_holdout.note: v33's published 79.51% and v34's 83.01% are on different holdouts and are not comparable. Only the 77.22% baseline in this block is.

seed_ensemble.reason: The k=6 z-score average lands below the best single seed and barely above the seed mean, so the generalisation gap is data-sample variance rather than fitting instability. This is what redirected v34 to data acquisition.

full_corpus.reason: Ties the 87.5% corpus on validation but its validation lead over test persists across the whole tree-count curve, unlike the 87.5% corpus which agrees to 0.07 points.

binary_labels.reason: 0.12 points below graded on validation. Note this is within noise: v33's +1.99 point graded advantage does not survive the enlarged corpus and the corrected tree count.

uniform_recency.reason: 0.35 points below the v33 recency weight on validation.

ndcg_early_stopping.reason: The stopping metric (NDCG over graded labels) is not the deployed metric (strict Top-1), and the stopping point is resampled per fit, so corpus comparisons were dominated by it. Removing it exposed that 1005 trees was badly undertrained.

safety_guards: Always preserve a deterministic immediate lethal attack.
Reject candidates that destroy a currently available KO.
Never end the turn while the Active Alakazam can attack.
Do not cycle Dudunsparce away from a board of two or fewer Pokemon.
Use the frozen v29 policy for unsupported, nested, low-time, or illegal cases.

inference_cost.measured_on: 289 scoped holdout decisions with teacher memory disabled
inference_cost.note: Trees are 2.04x but wall clock is 1.46x because feature construction is shared. Selection and fallback rates are identical to v33, so the safety behaviour is unchanged. Not yet measured on the real ladder.

ladder_behaviour_diagnosis.source: All replays of the existing v31/v32/v33 ladder runs
ladder_behaviour_diagnosis.reading: Powerful Hand count is the only measure that separates wins from losses (27% below four, 81% at four or more). The Dudunsparce usage gap recorded earlier is closed: win rate is now flat across usage buckets, so that lever is spent. v34's largest offline gain is the evolve class (+11.91 points), which is the class that puts Alakazam on the board, but the causal link to Powerful Hand count on the ladder is unproven.

known_limitations: The requested 90% unseen Top-1 agreement was not reached. The best deployable strict held-out Top-1 is 83.01%.
Not yet submitted to the ladder. Every strength claim here is offline agreement, and v33 demonstrated that agreement and rating are only weakly related (Top-1 +0.80 for rating +35.7).
v33's published 79.51% and v34's 83.01% are on different holdouts and cannot be compared directly. Only the 77.22% same-holdout baseline is comparable.
The 46.4% inference increase has not been measured on the real ladder.
Boss's Orders agreement is 47.94%, the lowest of any action class, on 194 decisions.
The trainer class (n=1843, 70.48%) is the largest absolute source of remaining error.
The 87.5% truncation ties the full corpus on validation to within 0.05 points; it was chosen on validation/test agreement, not on a significant single-metric difference.
The Kaggle EpisodeService returns only the most recent 1,000 episodes per submission, so teacher logs are lost unless refetched periodically.
